statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-22693 (GHSA-xvjr-f2r9-c7ww): SubtableUnicodesCache::create() in src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh constructs an object in the result of hb_malloc() without checking for NULL, so an allocation failure while building the subsetter's cmap cache dereferences a null pointer and crashes. HarfBuzz fixed it in commit https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/commit/1265ff8d990284f04d8768f35b0e20ae5f60daae, released in 12.3.0. Alpine lists harfbuzz in 3.23 as possibly vulnerable, with no fixed version (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-22693). The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes harfbuzz 12.2.0-r0 and 12.2.0-r1 on x86_64 and aarch64. We disassembled libharfbuzz-subset.so from both builds on both architectures. In 12.2.0-r1, as in 12.2.0-r0, the inlined cache allocation stores into the 64-byte block returned by hb_malloc() with no null test. The machine code of libharfbuzz.so and libharfbuzz-subset.so is identical between the two builds on each architecture, so neither carries the fix. Every published build of this owner is affected.

CVE-2026-22693 (GHSA-xvjr-f2r9-c7ww): SubtableUnicodesCache::create() in src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh constructs an object in the result of hb_malloc() without checking for NULL, so an allocation failure while building the subsetter's cmap cache dereferences a null pointer and crashes. HarfBuzz fixed it in commit https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/commit/1265ff8d990284f04d8768f35b0e20ae5f60daae, released in 12.3.0. Debian backported the fix to trixie in harfbuzz 10.2.0-1+deb13u1 (Debian bug #1125189), and the Debian tracker lists that version as fixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-22693). This owner is built from Debian 10.2.0-1+deb13u1. The DHI Debian repository publishes two rebuilds of that version on amd64 and arm64, and no build of an earlier Debian version. The changelog both rebuilds ship lists the CVE-2026-22693 entry from 10.2.0-1+deb13u1. In the amd64 libharfbuzz-subset.so of both rebuilds, the cache allocation tests the malloc() result before using it. The range closes at the first of the two rebuilds, so every published build reads as fixed.
